questions.question: What defines pluripotent embryonic stem cells compared to multipotent adult stem cells?
options: Pluripotent stem cells can differentiate into almost any cell type derived from all three germ layers, whereas multipotent stem cells are committed to a limited lineage
Pluripotent stem cells cannot undergo continuous mitotic division in cell culture
Multipotent stem cells can differentiate into entire functional extraembryonic placental tissues
Pluripotent stem cells contain only half the diploid number of chromosomes
questions.explanation: Pluripotent stem cells (e.g. from the blastocyst inner cell mass) can form cells from ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. Multipotent stem cells (e.g., hematopoietic bone marrow cells) can only produce cells of a specific related lineage.
questions.citation: IB Biology Subject Guide — Topic 1.1: Introduction to Cells

questions.question: When plant tissue is placed in a hypertonic sucrose solution with a more negative water potential than the cytoplasm, what physiological event occurs?

The cell becomes fully turgid as water rushes into the central vacuole down its osmotic gradient
The cell bursts due to osmotic lysis because plant cell walls cannot withstand tensile tension

questions.question: During agarose gel electrophoresis of restriction-digested DNA fragments, why do smaller DNA fragments migrate faster towards the positive anode (+)?

Smaller DNA fragments possess a higher net positive charge than larger fragments
Agarose gel pores selectively bind larger nucleotide bases like adenine and guanine
DNA ligase actively propels smaller fragments towards the electrode

questions.question: For each turn of the citric acid (Krebs) cycle within the mitochondrial matrix, what are the total products generated from one acetyl-CoA (2C) molecule?
options: 2 CO2, 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 ATP (via GTP)
1 CO2, 2 NADH, 2 FADH2, and 2 ATP
3 CO2, 1 NADH, 3 FADH2, and 0 ATP
4 CO2, 4 NADH, 0 FADH2, and 4 ATP
questions.explanation: One acetyl-CoA combines with oxaloacetate (4C) to form citrate (6C). During two oxidative decarboxylations and further dehydrogenations, 2 CO2 are released, 3 NAD+ are reduced to NADH, 1 FAD is reduced to FADH2, and 1 ATP/GTP is formed by substrate-level phosphorylation.

questions.question: Which morphological adaptation minimizes transpirational water loss in xerophytic desert plants like Marram grass (Ammophila arenaria)?
options: Rolled leaves with sunken stomata situated in interior microcrypts protected by epidermal trichomes (hairs)
Extremely thin cuticles with broad flattened lamina to maximize radiant cooling
High density of stomata exclusively on the upper adaxial leaf surface
Permanent daytime opening of stomata coupled with total absence of root endodermis
questions.explanation: Marram grass rolls its leaves, trapping moist air in the inner core. Sunken stomata located in hair-lined pits create localized microclimates of high humidity, dramatically decreasing the water vapor concentration gradient and transpirational flux.

questions.question: How does phytochrome control flowering in short-day (long-night) plants?
options: Active phytochrome Pfr acts as an inhibitor of flowering; during long uninterrupted nights, Pfr slowly reverts to inactive Pr, removing the inhibition and allowing flowering
Pr absorbs far-red light and directly stimulates flowering promoter genes at noon
Pfr accumulates during long nights and stimulates florigen synthesis in root meristems
Short-day plants flower only when night length is repeatedly interrupted by brief red light flashes
questions.explanation: Phytochrome exists in two interconvertible forms: Pr (absorbs red light ~660 nm, converting to Pfr) and Pfr (absorbs far-red light ~730 nm, slowly reverting to Pr in darkness). In short-day plants, Pfr is an inhibitor of flowering. A long uninterrupted darkness period allows Pfr to drop below the threshold, triggering flowering.

questions.question: What structural feature of an immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody molecule enables it to bind specifically to two identical epitopes simultaneously on a pathogen?
options: A bivalent Y-shaped quaternary structure with two identical variable antigen-binding sites (Fab fragments) formed by the heavy and light chains
A single constant domain containing four allosteric catalytic protease sites
A circular carbohydrate ring surrounded by eight identical Fc fragments
Disulfide bonds that crosslink with host erythrocyte hemoglobin
questions.explanation: An antibody consists of 4 polypeptide chains (2 heavy, 2 light) linked by disulfide bonds into a Y-shape. The tips of the Y form two hypervariable antigen-binding regions (Fab), conferring bivalent specificity.

questions.subtopic: Topic 11: Animal Physiology (Ultrafiltration in the Glomerulus)
questions.question: Which anatomical barrier in the renal corpuscle prevents albumin and other large plasma proteins from passing into the glomerular filtrate in Bowman's capsule?
options: The negatively charged basement membrane (lamina densa) and filtration slits between podocyte pedicels
The microvilli of the loop of Henle thin descending limb
The endothelial tight junctions of the vasa recta capillaries
The dense muscular sphincter of the macula densa
questions.explanation: Glomerular ultrafiltration is mediated by a 3-layer barrier: fenestrated capillary endothelium, the negatively charged basement membrane (which electrostatically repels negative plasma proteins like albumin), and interdigitating podocyte filtration slits.

questions.subtopic: Topic 11: Animal Physiology (Countercurrent Multiplier in Loop of Henle)
questions.question: Why is the descending limb of the loop of Henle permeable to water but impermeable to sodium chloride, while the ascending limb is impermeable to water and actively pumps sodium chloride?
options: To establish a steep hypertonic osmotic gradient in the medullary interstitium, enabling maximum passive water reabsorption from the collecting duct
To neutralize acidic glomerular filtrate before it enters the renal pelvis
To pump glucose into the renal cortex against steep diffusion gradients
To dilute urine into hypotonic sweat for cutaneous excretion
questions.explanation: The countercurrent multiplier system creates an increasing osmotic gradient in the renal medulla (up to ~1200 mOsm/L). The active transport of Na+ and Cl- out of the thick ascending limb without water creates hypertonicity, drawing water out of the descending limb and collecting duct.

questions.question: How does human oogenesis differ fundamentally from spermatogenesis in terms of meiotic timing and cellular yield?
options: Oogenesis produces one functional ovum and polar bodies through unequal cytokinesis, with meiosis arrested in Prophase I until puberty, whereas spermatogenesis continuously produces four equal functional spermatozoa
Oogenesis begins at puberty and produces four functional gametes per primary oocyte
Spermatogenesis arrests in Metaphase II during embryonic fetal life until copulation
Oogenesis proceeds without meiotic crossing over or chiasmata formation
questions.explanation: Oogenesis starts before birth (primary oocytes arrest in Prophase I until puberty). Each cycle, one oocyte resumes meiosis, arresting at Metaphase II until fertilization, producing only 1 mature ovum and 2-3 non-functional polar bodies due to unequal cytoplasmic division.

questions.subtopic: Topic 11: Animal Physiology (Cortical Reaction & Polyspermy Prevention)
questions.question: What is the biochemical mechanism of the cortical reaction in the ovum following sperm fusion?
options: Cortical granules release enzymes via exocytosis that digest sperm-binding receptors and harden the zona pellucida, permanently preventing polyspermy
Rapid influx of potassium ions hyperpolarizes the vitelline membrane, attracting additional sperm nuclei
The ovum discharges maternal lysosomes into the perivitelline space to hydrolyze the male pronucleus
The corona radiata forms an impermeable chitin shell within 5 milliseconds
questions.explanation: Sperm-egg fusion triggers an intracellular Ca2+ wave that prompts cortical granules to fuse with the egg plasma membrane. Their exocytosed proteases destroy ZP3 receptors and cross-link glycoproteins, hardening the zona pellucida into an impenetrable fertilization envelope (slow block to polyspermy).
